Omar: FYI - after landing runtime change in PR #4021 we started seeing an increased p50 tail on long sequences (8k tokens). I ran quick nsys and perfetto captures, attaching links to the raw traces: /artifacts/nsys/2262504123-before.qdrep and /artifacts/nsys/2262504123-after.qdrep

Julia: Ugh, thanks. Is that p50 for the whole request or for token emit? Any delta in kernel counts?

Omar: token emit. End-to-end p50 up ~8% on our 8k benchmark. Kernel timeline shows more frequent kernel switching around the KV-cache warmup boundary. Snapshot from perfetto: `batcher_hold -> kernel_switch -> memcopy` loop increased.

Ryan: Can you paste the kernel chooser log? wondering if a different kernel variant is being picked mid-sequence.

Omar: copy of nvtx region from the after trace:
```
NVTX: batcher.enter
CUDA: launch kernel=gpt_attention_fused_F32 grid=(...) time=1.9ms
CUDA: launch kernel=gpt_attention_prefetch grid=(...) time=0.6ms
CUDA: launch kernel=gpt_attention_qkv_qint8 grid=(...) time=2.3ms
NVTX: batcher.exit
```
Note the chooser switches between the fused F32 and the qint8 variant in adjacent tokens. Not sure why.

Sasha: Is this correlated with the batching heuristic change in #4021? That PR adjusted the batcher scheduler to prefer earlier flushes on slot contention. Could be increasing boundary churn.

Omar: I ran a git-bisect-ish test. Bisect points to commit 8f7a3b2 (the scheduler tweak) as first bad. Reproducer run commands I used:
```
# reproducer (local)
./bench/run_infer --model rwd-small --seq 8192 --batcher-config conf/batcher_sched.json --runs 20
nsys profile -o before.qdrep --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx ./bench/run_infer ...
```

perf-bot: nsys job complete: /artifacts/nsys/2262504123-after.qdrep (1.2GB). Perfetto UI link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/2262504123-after

Julia: Ok looks like the scheduler now aggressively flushes groups when slot_wait > 250us which increases the number of flush events. That can cause extra kernel-selection work because the runtime recomputes the kernel variant on a per-flush basis. Two ideas: (1) increase the slot_wait threshold back to 500us in a canary; (2) memoize kernel selection per-model+seq_len for short windows.

Ryan: From the traces I see a KV-cache miss spike aligned with the flushes. Each flush triggers a small memcopy to refill KV buffers and that pushes the kernel chooser to the slow path (cache miss -> fallback variant). The memcopy shows up as `cudaMemcpyAsync` ~300-600us bursts.

Omar: I reproduced locally with a simple patch that disables the new aggressive flush and p50 returns to baseline. Will open a revert PR if we agree. I also captured an nvprof style sampling to compare hotspots (nvprof_out.txt): `/artifacts/nvprof/2262504123-sample.txt`.

Sasha: Can you attach a small perfetto heatmap png for before/after? visual helps PMs.

Omar: added small screenshots to the artifact bucket: `/artifacts/plots/2262504123-heatmap-before.png` and `/artifacts/plots/2262504123-heatmap-after.png`. The after heatmap has noticeably more short-lived kernel slices (fanned pattern).

Julia: Proposed plan: (A) revert the aggressive flush change for canary (fast rollback), (B) add a cheap kernel-selection memoization keyed by (model_version, seq_bucket, device_mem_state) with a 50ms TTL, (C) add a test that runs the 8k sequence benchmark in CI to catch regressions. Anyone object?

Ryan: +1 to all. Add a metric during rollout: count(kernel_variant_switches) per-request. That'll flag future churn.

Sasha: I'll file a short incident note and tag PMs, include the heatmaps.

Omar: Opening PRs now: revert -> #4080, memoize -> #4081, ci-benchmark -> #4082. Will monitor after revert canary.

perf-bot: canary deploy finished: deploy/karma-4 -> success (10% traffic). Metrics dashboard: https://dash.redwood/kanary/4021-canary

Julia: After canary smoke: initial numbers look good, kernel_switch metric down ~70% in canary. Let's keep canary for 2 hours then decide. :thumbsup:

Omar: thanks all, I'll follow up with postmortem if canary confirms.
